chunks: I was between Mecca and Medina, I and a companion of mine. We discussed the Ansar; one of us said they were drawn from various tribes, and one of us said they were from the people of Yemen.

Then we arrived at Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was sitting in the shade of a tree. He began the hadith without our asking. He said: When Tubba' came from the direction of Iraq, with scholars and sons of the prophets in his company,

When he reached the valley of Hudhayl, some people from certain tribes came to him and said: You are coming to the people of a town who have been playing games with people for a long time, until they made their land a haram and their building a lord or goddess. He said: If things are as you say, I will kill their fighters, enslave their descendants, and demolish their building. His two eyes then flowed down until they fell onto his cheeks. Then he summoned the scholars and sons of the prophets.

He said: Examine my case and inform me why this has befallen me. They refused to tell him until he firmly pressed them. They said: Tell us what you said to yourself. He said: I said to myself that I would kill their fighters, enslave their descendants, and demolish their building. They said: We see nothing that has befallen you except because of that. He asked: And why is that? They said: Because the city —

— is the haram of Allah, the House is the House of Allah, and its inhabitants are the descendants of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful. He said: You have spoken truly. What is my way out of what I have fallen into? They said: Turn your thoughts to something else; perhaps Allah will restore it to you. He turned his thoughts to good, and they returned.

His irises returned until they settled back in their place. He summoned the people who had advised him to demolish it and executed them. Then he came to the House, covered it, and provided food for thirty days — one hundred camels each day — until the bowls were carried to the wild beasts on the mountaintops and fodder was scattered in the valleys for the wildlife. Then he departed from Mecca to Medina and settled there a people from the people of Yemen, from Ghassan — and they are the Ansar.
[In another narration: he covered it with niṭa' cloth and perfumed it.]
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Ansar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) narrates the story of Tubba', a righteous ancient Yemeni king who came toward Mecca. When he rashly threatened to kill Mecca's defenders, enslave their descendants, and demolish the Ka'ba, his eyes flowed out onto his cheeks. The scholars and sons of prophets traveling with him told him this affliction was because the city is Allah's haram, the Ka'ba is Allah's House, and its people are descendants of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful. After repenting and reverting to good intention, his sight was restored. He covered the Ka'ba, fed its people for thirty days with one hundred camels daily, then departed and settled in Medina a Yemeni people from Ghassan — who became the Ansar.
